lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedThe Coup That Didn't TakeContestedItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: SEPTEMBER 1943: SPECULATIVE · filed with minor delayImmediate AftermathThis file closes on September 1943, a speculative branch's own ending rather than a date the documented record recognizes: six weeks of an Italian army fighting itself that the actual, bloodless transition of July 1943 never had to spend. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. A speculative path with almost no historical footing: the officer corps' actual loyalty to the constitutional monarchy in July 1943 proved deeper than any loyalty to Mussolini personally. What this file records instead is a counterfactual crisis of legitimacy inside the regime's own institutions: one the losing war underneath it would have overtaken regardless of who signed the orders. A deliberate early withdrawal from the Alamein line concedes the same ground the historical twelve-day battle eventually lost anyway, without first spending the attritional casualties a fuel-starved defense was never favored to hold.
